statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail has crossed the block threshold on an observed failed retracement and extension to the session low.

headline: Semiconductor-led break to the session low lifts Tail into the block band even as yields, oil and Iran headlines ease
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index trades at 30,580.58, down 579.49 points or 1.86%, and is printing the low of its 30,580.58 to 31,125.13 session range against a 31,160.08 previous close. Nasdaq-100 December futures, the preferred continuous reference, are at 30,949.25, down 1.44%, about 41 points above their own 30,908.50 session low. The decisive feature of this hour is the sequence rather than the level: NBC News reporting updated at 12:58 ET described equities at their best levels of the day with the S&P 500 down only 0.2%, and the verified quotes taken at 13:16 to 13:26 ET then show the Nasdaq-100 down 1.86% at a new session low. That is an observed failed retracement followed immediately by extension, with price sitting at the extreme and no recovery yet visible. Semiconductors are the clear leader: the PHLX Semiconductor Index is at 12,490.16, down 575.99 points or 4.41%, effectively at its 12,489.84 session low, against a 13,066.15 previous close. What makes this assessment a genuine step up rather than a continuation of the earlier rates-and-oil narrative is that the macro amplifier stack has unwound while equities fell. The 17:00Z sale of $22 billion in 30-year bonds was solid, stopping at 5.618% against a 5.617% when-issued level with a 2.54 bid-to-cover versus a 2.41 average, 72.32% indirect takedown and only 6.79% left with dealers. The 10-year yield is 5.24%, down 3 basis points and off its 5.33% intraday high, which NBC describes as the lowest level since Monday. WTI is at $90.87, up 2.93% but well below its $93.20 high, after the US President posted that there would be no attack on Iran before the November 3 midterm elections, although the blockade of Iranian ports reportedly remains in force. Initial jobless claims for the week ended 3 October printed 197,000 against a 200,000 consensus. The decline is therefore an idiosyncratic semiconductor and AI de-rating rather than a cross-asset risk event, and the absence of aligned amplifiers caps how far Tail can justifiably rise. VIX at 15.92, up 5.57% from 15.08, is historically low and shows no protection panic alongside a 1.86% index decline. Tail is set at 28, inside the block band, because the observed failed-retracement-then-extension pattern with the index at a session extreme and semiconductors down 4.41% is precisely the path structure Tail measures, while the easing rates, oil and geopolitical inputs together with subdued implied volatility argue against the higher band. Stress rises to 72 on the depth of the semiconductor drawdown. The flagged window runs to the 20:30Z post-close settle, after which the forecast decays as liquidity thins, with the Asian chip complex the named checkpoint overnight.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours opened with a quiet mean-reverting overnight tape in which Tail decayed from 17 to a low of 10 by 03:00Z while Stress drifted in a 47 to 53 range. From 06:00Z the oil and long-end-yield impulse took over: Tail stepped to 22 at 07:00Z and then held a 20 to 23 watch-band range through the European and early US session, with Stress climbing from 55 to a 65 to 66 plateau from 11:00Z onward. The 14:00Z slot briefly eased to Tail 17 as the US cash open proved orderly, before 15:00Z and 16:00Z returned to 20 and 22. Dominant mode was mixed throughout apart from trend-down readings at 06:00Z, 07:00Z and 11:00Z. No hour in the window reached the block threshold, which is the specific change introduced by the current assessment. No published hour is rewritten here.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in the 26 to 29 block band across the remainder of the US cash session, peaking at 29 in the 19:00Z power hour because the index would enter that window at a session extreme, then easing to 26 at the 20:00Z close as index rebalancing completes. Tail returns to the watch band at 22 post-close and decays to a cycle low of 18 between 04:00Z and 05:00Z as liquidity thins and the easing rates and oil backdrop reduces amplifier alignment. The named overnight checkpoint is the Asian handover: the 00:00Z and 01:00Z slots are held at 20 and 21 because Tokyo and Seoul cash trading in the memory and foundry complex prices today's 4.41% SOX decline for the first time, and a chip-led Asian second leg is the stated escalation mechanism. Risk then rebuilds modestly through the European session from 19 at 06:00Z to the watch band at 20, before stepping to 22 at the 13:00Z approach to the US cash open and a forward peak of 23 at 14:00Z, when preliminary Michigan sentiment prints and its inflation-expectation components carry added weight after Brent traded as high as $105.92 today. Stress tracks the same shape at a higher level, easing from 73 to 55 overnight and rebuilding to 63. Confidence decays monotonically from 85 to 70 with distance from the verified observations. The stated invalidations are a reclaim of the earlier 30,918 low area, an orderly two-sided close, or conversely a close printed on the session low. All forward values are conditional risk and not an assertion that future price structure has been observed.

forecast.analysis: Observed: the Nasdaq-100 cash index trades at 30,580.58, -1.86%, exactly at its session low after reaching the day's best levels near 12:58 ET and immediately failing.
